description: We’re Dettol Warriors, a team building a Space Mission Design Game for NASA Space Apps. Our strengths are programming, physics, and aerospace systems. Players pick spacecraft components, balance mass, power, and cost budgets using real mission data, and launch a lunar orbiter. A post-mission report shows which trade-offs led to success or failure.
summary: we built a browser based space game that turns real mission challenges into hands on and exciting gameplay. Instead of reading through dense facts, players jump straight into simulated space scenarios where they intially have to manage technical details of the space mission and keep finances, weight and other metrics in mind. thet have to think fast and solve problems on the fly. Our goal was to make space exploration feel exciting and easy to grasp for anyone, regardless of their science background. By combining simple controls with interactive challenges, incredible graphics and a fun customisable expierence; the game gets people—especially students—genuinely curious about how space missions work and why solving these problems matters or how much goes into these missisons.
details: Our project is an interactive, browser-based space mission simulator that puts players in charge of planning and executing real space operations. starting with managing strict technical constraints like payload weight, budget, and engineering specs before jumping into fast-paced, real-time gameplay where they must react quickly and solve mission-critical problems on the fly. Built using HTML5 Canvas, CSS3, JavaScript, and React—and hosted live on Netlify so anyone can play instantly without downloads—the game transforms complex aerospace logistics into an intuitive, customizable experience with clean visuals and responsive controls. Our goal is to bridge the gap between textbook STEM concepts and hands-on intuition, giving students and everyday players a fun, accessible way to appreciate the immense engineering, strategy, and problem-solving required behind every real-world space mission.
